title: NEMAR MetricSnapshot
description: Versioned contract for the NEMAR observability dashboard. Mirror of src/lib/schema.ts (Zod is the SOURCE OF TRUTH; this file is documentation). The push endpoint (/api/sections/:key) expects a $defs/sectionIngest body (a section WITHOUT updated_at, which the server stamps). Note: Zod strips unknown fields at the section and metric level rather than rejecting them, so a payload with extra fields there is accepted (the extras dropped) even though additionalProperties is false here. The exceptions are `daily_series` and `channel_hours` with everything nested inside them, which are strict: an unknown key is rejected with 422 (an unknown key could be a dataset identifier). A producer that adds a field to `channel_hours` needs the Worker deployed first.

section_errors.description: Built-in sections that failed to compute this run (absent when all succeeded).

dailySeries.description: Cross-field rules also enforced by the section-ingest endpoint's Zod validator: coverage_start must not follow coverage_end, point dates must be unique, and every point date must fall within declared coverage. Standard JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness by one object property or compare these instance fields, so non-TypeScript producers must enforce these three rules before POSTing.

points.description: Dates must be unique and within coverage; values are finite non-negative additive observations. Missing dates are unknown, not zero. uniqueItems rejects identical points; the API additionally rejects repeated dates with different values.

channels.description: Exact channel count of the recordings in this bin.

hours.description: Summed recording time, in hours. Zero is legal (a measured recording can have no duration).

recordings.description: Bins are sparse: only channel counts that occur are present.

datasets.description: Datasets whose largest recording in this modality has exactly this many channels.

channelHoursModality.description: Cross-field rules also enforced by the Zod validator: bins and dataset_peaks are strictly ascending by channels (so counts are unique); every dataset peak has a bin at its channel count and holds no more datasets than that bin has recordings; the largest peak and the largest bin are at the same channel count; recordings equals the sum over bins; hours equals the sum over bins within max(1e-6, hours * 1e-9) (round each bin first, then sum the rounded bins); datasets equals the sum over dataset_peaks.

modality.description: Stable key and display name, e.g. EEG, iEEG, MEG, EMG: a plain name. Unique per section, case-insensitive.

channelHours.description: Recorded hours by channel count, per modality, over public datasets only (no dataset identifiers). Recordings that lack a duration or channel count are counted in recordings_unmeasured and left out of every bin. Modality names are unique case-insensitively and no modality may report more datasets than datasets_scanned. The array bounds are headroom: the 1 MB push body cap is the effective size limit.

drilldown.description: Admin drill-down key resolving to the list behind the number

breakdown_unit.description: Unit of the breakdown values when it differs from `unit` (e.g. a count of datasets broken down by bytes each). Falls back to `unit` when absent.

breakdown_style.description: How to draw the breakdown: 'bars' for a distribution (default), 'ranked' for an ordered top-N list where a bar would merely restate the printed value.

source.description: Producer id: nemar-cli, access, or a pipeline id

layout.description: Tile arrangement. 'split' pairs a wide distribution with a narrow companion list. Layout hint only; consumers may ignore it.

sectionIngest.description: POST /api/sections/:key body: a section WITHOUT updated_at (server-stamped), no larger than 1 MB. `key` must equal the URL :key and must not be a built-in (datasets|archive|zarr|sync|publication|access|users). Optional daily_series are additive UTC count/byte observations, separate from headline metrics. Limits: 16 series and 5000 daily points per section; 3660 points per series.
